title: Transfer RNA (tRNA)
subject: Biochemistry & genetics
summary: tRNA translates mRNA codons into amino acids during protein synthesis. It carries specific amino acids, recognizes codons via anticodons, and is charged by aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetases. Defects cause metabolic and neuro‑developmental disorders.

sections.p: tRNA is a small RNA that bridges the genetic code and protein synthesis. Each tRNA has a variable loop, an anticodon loop, and a CCA‑3′ end that accepts an amino acid.

Aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetases attach the correct amino acid to the 3′‑CCA end of tRNA. The charged tRNA enters the ribosome A‑site, pairs its anticodon with the mRNA codon, and the peptidyl transferase centre links the amino acid to the growing peptide.

t.b: Assesses enzyme expression in patient samples

sections.p: tRNA levels are controlled by transcription, processing, and degradation. Stress or nutrient deprivation can alter tRNA abundance and modify codon usage bias.
b: Processing by RNase P and Z

sections.p: Mutations in tRNA genes or in aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetases lead to metabolic disorders, neuro‑developmental delay, and mitochondrial disease.

t.b: Shows basal ganglia hyperintensity in Leigh syndrome
Ringed sideroblasts indicate tRNA‑related sideroblastic anaemia

sections.p: In low‑resource settings, tRNA‑related disorders may present as unexplained failure to thrive, developmental delay, or recurrent infections. Diagnosis relies on clinical suspicion and basic labs.
b: Elevated lactate in blood or CSF

sections.p: Remember the key steps: aminoacylation, anticodon‑codon pairing, ribosomal sites (A, P, E). In exams, focus on enzyme defects and their clinical syndromes.
b: Aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetase defects cause multisystem disease

sections.p: tRNA is distinct from mRNA (messenger) and rRNA (ribosomal). It is not a transporter protein.
Low tRNA levels may be masked by compensatory upregulation of other tRNAs; enzyme assays can be falsely normal if the mutation affects regulation rather than activity.
b: Enzyme activity may appear normal in heterozygotes

sections.p: Treat underlying metabolic defect if identified; supportive care includes nutritional support, antioxidants, and avoiding metabolic stressors. Monitor growth, neurodevelopment, and organ function.
Urgent referral if patient shows acute neurological decline, lactic acidosis, or multi‑organ failure.

t.a: What is the role of initiator tRNA?
t.b: It delivers formyl‑methionine to start protein synthesis
Aminoacyl‑tRNA synthetases esterify amino acids to tRNA
Rarely, via mitochondrial dysfunction leading to oxidative stress

exam: 1. A 3‑year‑old presents with failure to thrive and lactic acidosis. What enzyme defect should you suspect? — Look for tRNA^Leu(UUR) mutation causing Leigh syndrome; check MRI and lactate. 2. Which step in translation involves the A‑site of the ribosome? — Entry of elongator tRNA carrying the next amino acid. 3. A patient has a missense mutation in the gene for methionyl‑tRNA synthetase. What clinical features are likely? — Neuro‑developmental delay, hypotonia, possible catar
